title: Catalyst bridge daily queue & runbook notes
content:
Shift: 09:00-17:00 PDT (Catalyst bridge)
Owner: Aisha Patel -> handing off to Liam Chen at 17:00 PDT
Slack channel: #sre-catalyst (watch), escalation lane #oncall-escalate
Summary (high level):
- Quiet start, followed by two short bursts of 95th percentile latency on /v1/generate at ~11:18 and ~14:02 (peak ~650ms, baseline ~120ms).
- An increase in 5xx rate for the embeddings service from 0.1% -> 1.2% between 13:55-14:10. Root cause suspected as ephemeral Redis GC spikes coincident with autoscaling events.
- One customer-impacting ticket opened (JIRA-OPS-1482) for degraded throughput on a Dedicated pool in us-west1.
- No active incidents at handoff, mitigation tasks are in progress and owners assigned.
Top incidents / timeline:
- 11:18 — latency spike on /v1/generate (short, ~3m). Observed by synthetic pings. Quick triage: increased queue length on model-serving pods; autoscaler lagged by ~80s. Action: bumped pod target by +20% for the affected deployment. Follow-up: investigate HPA scale-up policy (ticket: JIRA-OPS-1490). Owner: Marisol (due 2028-07-18).
- 13:55 — 5xx spike in embeddings-service. Errors were predominantly Redis connection timeouts (context: connection pool exhaustion during scheduled background cache warm). Mitigation: temporarily increased Redis maxclients and rolled the warm job to staggered windows. Current state: error rate back to baseline as of 14:20. Follow-ups: improve runbook for background warm jobs and add circuit-breaker to embeddings-service client. Owner: Ethan (PR referenced above).
- 15:40 — Dedicated pool us-west1 reduced throughput (customer report JIRA-OPS-1482). Early signs: noisy neighbor on the same host node causing OOM kills of auxiliary processes and elevated p99 CPU. We moved the affected workloads to a different host and enabled emergency anti-affinity. Follow-up: scheduler heuristics tuning (deep-dive meeting scheduled 2028-07-16). Owner: Aisha.
Operational notes & metrics observed:
- SLOs: All core serving SLOs met overall for the shift, however latency SLIs showed 95th spikes tied to scale-up windows.
- Observability: missing traces on several 14:00 error samples — tracing agent dropped due to transient proxy restart (see logs: proxy-logs-2028-07-14-14:02). Action: increase trace agent restartbackoff; ticket JIRA-OPS-1494.
- Capacity: Redis avg memory 72% across cluster; one shard at 86% during spike. Consider incremental eviction threshold changes.
Runbook drafts and runbook deltas (in-shift edits):
- RUNBOOK DRAFT: redis-eviction-and-warmup.md (short summary appended below) — created a checklist for staggered warm jobs, recommended maxclients baseline and connection pool sizing per language binding. Please review before finalizing.
  - Quick steps for immediate mitigation:
    1) Scale up read-replica count by +1 for affected shard.
    2) Throttle warm job to 10% concurrency and retry with exponential backoff.
    3) If connection timeouts persist, add temporary routing to read-only fallback pool.
  - Notes: Aim to remove ad-hoc warm jobs in favor of orchestrated warm window in infra repo.
- RUNBOOK DELTA: model-autoscale-tuning.md — added a section to recommend target CPU-based HPA trigger + buffer for cold-started caches. Example values included; needs load-profile validation.
Outstanding follow-ups (action items):
- JIRA-OPS-1490: HPA scale-up thresholds analysis (Marisol) — gather 7-day histograms of queue length and scale event lag. Due 2028-07-18.
- JIRA-OPS-1494: tracing-agent restartbackoff increase and integration test (Ethan) — add synthetic trace assertions to CI. Due 2028-07-17.
- JIRA-OPS-1482 follow-up (Aisha) — deep-dive on scheduler anti-affinity ticket; document mitigation pattern for Dedicated pools. Meeting set 2028-07-16 10:00 PDT.
- Runbook review: redis-eviction-and-warmup.md (team review requested) — comments welcome in Confluence page by 2028-07-20.
Notes to incoming on-call (Liam):
- Watch the embedding-service traces around 03:00 UTC (midnight maintenance window) — we suspect a scheduled warm job runs near that time and can cause visible tail latency.
- Keep an eye on host-level OOMs in us-west1 for the next 48 hours while scheduler anti-affinity is being tuned. Alert: host-oom-warning (alert policy) currently fires w/ 3min delay — consider lowering to 1m if we continue to see regressions.
- If you receive a customer ticket referencing 'throughput regression', escalate to on-call pager immediately and ping #platform-eng for scheduler correlation.
Minor housekeeping and notes:
- Cleaned up two stale alerts this shift: redis-high-conns-dupe and model-cache-miss-legacy; created replacements with clearer thresholds.
- Added a short blurb to the SRE runbooks index noting that background warm jobs must be scheduled with jitter.
- Kudos: Marisol handled the HPA rollback cleanly and coordinated with infra.
Known unknowns / questions for SRE squad:
- Can infra provide a per-node noisy-neighbor score to preemptively migrate Dedicated pools? (Proposal: lightweight telemetry agent; add to backlog if feasible.)
- Should we adopt a default circuit-breaker in embeddings client libraries? (Pros/cons: quicker mitigation vs more complexity in client.)
Attachments / logs referenced:
- proxy-logs-2028-07-14-14:02 (stackdriver link in ticket JIRA-OPS-1494)
- redis-shard-7-metrics-2028-07-14.csv (uploaded to epic folder)
- heapdumps and pmap collection for the affected host (s3://redwood-ops/oom-dumps/2028-07-14/)
Handoff checklist (tick before close):
- [x] All active mitigation steps documented above
- [x] Owners assigned and tickets created
- [x] Immediate customer issues acknowledged and contacted
- [ ] Ensure runbook diffs are reviewed in 48h (assign reviewer)
If anything becomes urgent after handoff, call the on-call phone (primary): +1-415-555-0199 or escalate via pager.
Additional context / freeform notes:
- I started a short experiment to capture pre-scale state snapshots for 10s prior to HPA decisions (small script in infra repo). If useful, I can open a proper RFC.
- Leaving a TODO for the team to consider reducing the synthetic probe run frequency during known warm windows to avoid false positives on SLO dashboards.
End of shift.
Handed off at 17:00 PDT by Aisha Patel.
